1. SYNOPSIS > Study Design and Methodology:

Phase 1 is a multicenter, open-label, dose-ranging/dose-escalating study that will enroll up to 18 subjects.

A 3+3 design will be used for sequential dose-escalation cohorts in which subjects will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye on Day 1.

The final DSMB Meeting will be scheduled to review up-to-12-Month safety data for all fifty-one (51) subjects enrolled in Phase 2 part of the study.

DSMB Review Flow

To clarify further, the DSMB will systematically evaluate each group at these predefined intervals:

· First group (subjects #1-15): Safety reviewed at 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 9-month and 12-month intervals.

· Second group (subjects #16-30): Safety reviewed at 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 9-month and 12-month intervals.

· Third group (subjects #31-51): Safety reviewed at 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 9-month and 12-month intervals.

The assessments and measurements will be performed according to the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3).

Subjects are considered to have completed this study if they complete the End of Study (EOS) visit at month 12 after administration of IP. The study duration will be approximately 15 months for each subject (Screening through EOS visit).

Subjects randomized to the control group will be offered the opportunity to receive the study drug following database lock.

After the Phase 2 portion of the study has been unblinded and the full complement of safety and efficacy results have been evaluated, subjects in the control group may, at the discretion of the sponsor, enroll in an expansion protocol and receive the OCU410 treatment, provided they still meet all study eligibility criteria.

1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:

a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤ 20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one lesion must be ≥1.25 mm 2(0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy.

5. GA lesion within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging.

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN.

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.

10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.

Dosing eye recommendations for surgery will be made by PI and study surgeon by reviewing screening packet and on a case-by-case basis. This recommendation will be approved by the Sponsor. If a subject is diagnosed with wet AMD in the study eye or fellow eye at any point during the study, they will remain part of the study and must continue to follow the assessment schedule as outlined in the protocol.

5. Any ophthalmologic condition that reduces the clarity of the media and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents adequate imaging of the retina and interferes with ophthalmologic examination (e.g., advanced cataract or corneal abnormalities).

6. Have hypersensitivity to fluorescein or any contradiction for subretinal injection.

7. Aphakia, Cataract surgery or any other intraocular surgery (including lens replacement surgery) within 3 months (prior to Screening), YAG capsulotomy within 1-month, and any ophthalmic condition that may require surgery during the study period.

1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > Statistical Methods:

Primary Safety Endpoints

Adverse events (AEs) will be summarized using descriptive methods including counts and percentages by eye, dosage level, MedDRA classifications, severity, and relationship to study procedures; AEs will be defined as ocular or non-ocular for presentation.

Secondary Safety Endpoints

Secondary safety endpoints and the humoral and cellular immune response (anti-AAV5 antibodies, T-cell response) to OCU410 will be summarized using summary statistics, including minimum, 1st quartile, median, 3rd quartile, maximum, mean, and standard deviation.

Primary Efficacy Endpoint

Summary statistics, graphical displays, and statistical modeling approaches will be used as applicable to evaluate efficacy endpoints across timepoints, dosage levels and eye.

All tests are two-tailed with the type I error set at 10%. GA growth rates will be square-root transformed prior to analysis. The primary comparison of interest is the difference in the mean GA growth rates across both OCU410 dose groups versus the untreated control group at 1 year.

The mean growth rates of the individual OCU410 dose groups will be compared to controls and to each other. The type I error for these comparisons will be controlled using Tukey's HSD test. Growth rates and other continuous ophthalmic measures will be analyzed using a mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) methodology with treatment, time, and time by treatment considered as fixed factors and baseline value as a covariate. An unstructured covariance assumption will be used to model the within-subject correlation. Baseline values will be centered to their mean prior to inclusion in the model. The estimated mean change from baseline to 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48 weeks along with the respective 95% confidence intervals (CI) will be calculated from the model.

Exploratory Endpoints

Continuous ophthalmic measures will be analyzed in a similar manner as described for GA lesion size. The relative risk for conversion from dry to wet AMD will be computed along with its 95% CI.

table_headers: 6.4.1 Safety Criteria for Adjustment of Stopping Doses

Dose administration at the current level or dose-escalation will be terminated if either of the following are observed: · There are 2 similar SAEs or clinically significant AEs within the same cohort. · There are 3 or more similar AEs in this study that are deemed a medically unacceptable risk by the Investigator, the DSMB and the Sponsor.

The following stopping rules will be applied: . Occurrence of any Death · Occurrence of two or more Grade 3 and above systemic adverse events (CTCAE v.5) · Occurrence of two or more ocular adverse events that do not resolve within 14 days. Dose administration at the current level or dose-escalation will be paused and re- evaluated by the DSMB, Principal Investigator and the Sponsor. Next steps will be further decided based on their recommendations
Per FDA comments added additional stopping rules 38
